text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Communist Akel exploits the dispute between Diko party leader Spyros Kyprianou and Justice Minister Alecos Evangelou. Party chief Demetris Christofias urges Kyprianou to break his pact with the government.
- Man jailed for a series of burglaries threatened to kill the judge that sentenced him to five years in prison.
- Greek Ethnos newspaper speaks of tension in the Aegean and in Cyprus after Turkey's decision to create a crisis control centre in the eastern Aegean.
- Legislation is planned to curb clandestine trade from the north.
- Turkish shooting against British soldiers was "completely unjustifiable", the U.S. says.
- Auditor general reports millions are lost on tax and public works delays.
- Prices commission meets on Monday to discuss possible deregulation of prices of staple food items.
- The House of Representatives condemns the new bomb attack against a Limassol judge.
- The crisis in government deepens over Spyros Kyprianou's insistence that the justice minister be sacked.
- Greek and Cypriot engineers will test the resistance of buildings built before an anti-seismic code came into effect in 1986.
- Civil servants union Pasydy questions wisdom of government proposal to extend retirement age by three years to 63.
- President Glafcos Clerides has prepared a memorandum to be sent to Athens on the Greek Cypriot side's positions to views of Britain and the U.S. expressed on the Cyprus issue.
